transcript:
Header: Redwood All-Hands - March 31 2026
Start: 2026-03-31 10:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes | Recorded by: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Evelyn Park (CEO), Jordan Kim (CTO), Priya Rao (Head of Product), Diego Martinez (VP Eng), Samira Khan (Head of Research), Liam O'Connor (Head of Sales), Maya Lopez (CS) + company

[00:00] Evelyn Park: Good morning everyone, thanks for joining the March all-hands. we'll kick off with Q1 highlights, then Jordan and Diego will cover the Dedicated rollout and recent outage notes, Priya on product roadmap and Samira on research. Hoops as always keep questions to the end or drop in slack.

[00:32] Evelyn Park: Quick FYI, nice to see the energy, uh Q1 was solid — not perfect but solid. Revenue beat our internal plan by about 7%, org-wide utilization up, and we shipped the first Dedicated clusters to two customers in early access.

[01:05] Jordan Kim: Thanks Ev. Technical highlights — latency improvements from the kernel selector and batching changes are tracking: p50 down ~8% on common sequences, p95 improvements on streaming with the new async pipeline. We deployed the KV cache warm-up which helped cold-start cost by roughly 12%. There's still a bit of noise in longer-context runs.

[01:46] Jordan Kim: There was an outage on March 18th, brief recap — a regression in autoscaler heuristics combined with an edge case in fallback routing led to capacity blowouts for a handful of tenants. Diego will go through the root cause and mitigations in detail.

[02:10] Diego Martinez: Yeah, hi everyone. We traced the issue to an interaction between the autoscaler backoff timer and a mis-classified workload that triggered an aggressive scale-up loop. Essentially the system thought it needed GPU allocation and never re-balanced because the fallback policy didn't kick in due to a mismatch in model variant tags. It sounds nerdy but basically we overprovisioned for a short window.

[02:42] Diego Martinez: Immediate mitigations were: roll back the autoscaler change, add detection to the routing layer to flag rapid scale events, and a hotfix to ensure compatible variant fallback happens within 5s. Longer term: stronger integration tests and a canary for autoscaler heuristics.

[03:20] Evelyn Park: Thanks Diego. Important to call out the response was quick and SLA impact was limited, but customers did see elevated latencies. We're committed to a postmortem and a published runbook for customers so they understand what happened and what we're doing to prevent recurrence.

[03:54] Priya Rao: Product updates — Dedicated GA is on track for late Q2. We're prioritizing predictable throughput and improved UI for pinning model versions and rollout policies. Key asks from early access customers: simpler pricing buckets, clearer documentation for quantization profiles, and better logs for private deployments.

[04:25] Priya Rao: Also working on a lightweight onboarding flow for Dedicated where teams can import prompts and evaluation sets to measure quality/regressions before they flip to prod. This ties into Redwood Optimize — the suggestion engine will recommend batching/quantization by workload.

[05:00] Samira Khan: Research quick note — our eval framework picked up a couple of small regressions when we switched a kernel to a more aggressive fused-attention approach; we're tracking this as a model-regression signal within the QA harness. On private deployments, we have a test harness that runs locally against customer datasets (sanitized) to validate fidelity.

[05:35] Liam O'Connor: Sales highlights — closed two deals this quarter: BigBank (pilot for Dedicated + Private) and EduCo (hosted + optimize plan). BigBank's got heavy compliance asks — they wanted KMS, audit logs, and a VPC option; that's why Private push is getting momentum. Shoutout to Maya and the SEs, good work.

[06:02] Maya Lopez: On CS — onboarding churn improved, NPS is up 4 points year-over-year, but some new customers are asking for longer retention for trace logs (we need to weigh storage cost). Also seeing repeated feature request: per-route cost breakdown in console.

[06:30] Evelyn Park: Hiring and org — we are opening 25 new roles across infra, SDKs, and infra reliability; People Ops will share specifics. Reminder that we have a hiring freeze lift for a few strategic roles. Budget looks good for Q2 but we are watching ad spend and some discretionary items.

[07:05] Evelyn Park: Quick Q on branding — still Redwood Inference, but we're refining messages to emphasize 'production economics' in customer-facing comms.

[07:22] -- Slide change / internal notes omitted --

[07:45] (Audience question via Slack) "Can you share more detail on the Dedicated pricing model and SLA for GA?"

[08:02] Priya Rao: Short answer: pricing will be tiered (reserved v burst) with commit discounts; SLA target is 99.95 for Dedicated with latency SLOs per model class. We'll publish an FAQ next week. Pricing structure will be in bands to avoid microbilling complexity.

[08:35] (Murmurs) Someone: how about private pricing for on-prem?

[08:40] Evelyn Park: Private pricing will be enterprise license + support + optional deployment fees; it's flexible by region and compliance needs. We'll need RevOps and sales to collaborate on those deals.

[09:01] Jordan Kim: Back to outage: some of the transcribed logs are messy so apologies if the automatic notes show weird names — e.g., the autoscaler change was by "dev-3459" not a person. We're adding more human-friendly tags.

[09:18] Diego Martinez: Also the KV cache warm-up introduced a subtle ordering problem for certain prefix caching; patched today in staging. We'll monitor for any perf regressions.

[09:48] Samira Khan: Quick research highlight — released a new benchmark comparing quantization profiles across CPUs and H100s; results show that 4-bit quantization with our kernel set retains ~97% of baseline quality for short prompts. Caveat longer context still shows a gap.

[10:22] (Audience chat) "Any updates on SOC2 timeline?"

[10:30] Samira Khan: SOC2 in final audit phase, expect cert by mid-April; ISO conversation ongoing but lower priority right now. We'll publish compliance artifacts to the security portal.

[10:55] Evelyn Park: Customer stories — quick callout: BigBank pilot is promising. They were impressed by our routing policies and the private deployment checklist. Early feedback: they want clearer audit log retention options. Liam will follow up.

[11:20] Liam O'Connor: We're also tracking momentum with two other financials — one in EU asking about data residency, so region support is on the roadmap.

[11:45] Evelyn Park: OK let's do a lightning round — 30s each: what's the top focus for the next six weeks?

[12:00] Jordan Kim: Autoscaler stability and canary infra.

[12:10] Priya Rao: Dedicated launch comms and onboarding flows.

[12:20] Diego Martinez: Runbook and mitigation automation.

[12:30] Samira Khan: Finalize SOC2 artifacts and research-to-prod tests for quantization.

[12:40] Liam O'Connor: Close BigBank production deal and finish EU compliance answers.

[12:50] Maya Lopez: Improve onboarding checklist and per-route cost visibility.

[13:00] Evelyn Park: Alright, final notes — we'll circulate the Q1 deck, outage postmortem, and Dedicated FAQ early next week. thanks everyone, and a reminder: town hall Q&A on Friday for deeper product questions.

[13:20] (end)

Notes on transcription quality: automated; some speaker attributions generic; a few proper nouns may be mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes as "K V cash"). Links mentioned: Q1 deck (internal link), Dedicated FAQ (to be published), outage postmortem (to be shared).
